title: Telemetry-led tenant quarantine and reservation autosculpting
creator: Evan Zhou
description: Post-incident initiative to reduce dedicated-cluster capacity churn by introducing a telemetry-driven quarantine for noisy tenants and an autosculpting reservation adjuster. Goal: contain noisy behavior quickly (without full evictions), make reservation sizing resilient to transient spikes, and tune burst allowances to avoid cascading ejections. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, dashboards and a staged rollout with rollback criteria.
motivation: Recent capacity incidents showed repeated eviction storms when a small set of tenants produced pathological KV cache growth and long-running batched requests. Current reactive eviction and coarse reservation decay caused collateral damage. We need a surgical containment mechanism that uses live telemetry to throttle or quarantine misbehaving tenants and an autosculptor that smooths reservations based on short/medium-term signal windows.
design_notes: Introduce a tenant quarantine state separate from full eviction: soft-quarantine blocks new bursts and reduces burst tokens gradually while preserving in-flight requests for a short TTL (configurable 30-120s).

Autosculpting reservation controller operates on a two-window model: 1m short window for burst detection and 30m smoothing window for reservation adjustments; never reduce reservation by >20% per adjustment to avoid oscillation.

Telemetry signals: 95th/99th token latency, KV cache growth rate, GPU mem pressure, per-tenant concurrent streams, and sudden prefix miss spikes. Quarantine triggers when two signals cross thresholds within the short window.
Policy precedence: manual reservations and admin overrides always win; autosculpt only applies to dynamic reservations (not pinned capacity).
Fallback: if autosculpting causes SLA regressions for a tenant marked critical, automatic rollback of last change and alert to on-call.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy quarantine + autosculpt controller to canary cluster and run 72h soak without increased eviction rate vs baseline (target <10% change).
Quarantine correctly triggers on synthetic noisy tenants in staging (3 distinct signals firing) and reduces downstream eviction cascade in a reproducible test harness.
Reservation adjustments occur smoothly: smoothing window validation shows no >20% instantaneous reservation delta and 30m trending reduces incorrect oscillations in 90% of runs.
Dashboards: Datadog panel 'quota.autosculpt.events' and 'quarantine.actions' created and surface tenant, signal reasons, durations, and rollback occurrences.
Runbook updated with playbook steps for manual unquarantine, emergency evict, and autosculpt audit commands.
tasks: Write controller prototype and unit tests (controller/tenant_autosculpt.go).
Add signal collectors (telemetry exporters) and Datadog metrics (kv.growth_rate, tenant.burst_tokens, tenant.quarantine_state).
Integrate with reservation service API: dry-run, apply, and revert endpoints.
Create e2e synthetic noisy-tenant harness and baseline comparison tests in staging.
Build dashboards and SLO monitors; add alerts for false-positive quarantine rate >5% of quarantines in 24h.
Security review for control-plane changes and RBAC scoping for autosculpt endpoints.
Canary rollout: 5% of clusters -> 20% -> 100% with observability gates between steps.
Documentation: PRD -> Confluence design doc, runbook, API reference and changelog entry.
implementation_decisions: Use existing reservation-controller CRD for apply/revert flows to avoid a second actuator.
Prefer soft-quarantine over immediate evict: reduces user request failures while limiting resource consumption.
Autosculpt will be opt-in per-tenant initially to gather telemetry and avoid customer surprise; default off for enterprise pinned reservations.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): library-level unit tests and local end-to-end harness (complete).
Stage 1 (canary-staging): enable on staging cluster with 10 synthetic noisy tenants and validate containment (target window: 48h).
Stage 2 (canary-prod 5%): enable for non-enterprise tenants flagged experimental; monitor for 72h and check dashboards/gates.
Stage 3 (ramp): 20% -> 50% -> 100% with manual approvals at each gate and automated rollback triggers.
rollback_criteria: Increase in eviction rate >15% vs baseline for a 1h window after change
>=2 customer-impacting latency incidents attributable to autosculpt/quarantine in 24h
False-positive quarantine rate >5% of quarantines or unexplained quota drops for pinned tenants
